issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), but the problem specification (UML and task descriptions) and the solution implementation use a single-parameter signature addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in method signature is structural and will confuse students about which method they should implement and expect to be called by tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the UML and solution by changing the template method to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, if validation is required, provide an overloaded private helper or an internal boolean flag, but keep the public API matching the specification (single int parameter).

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution define an addGuestStudents method that takes a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)). The template, however, declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) — the extra boolean parameter changes the method signature and the conceptual mapping for the same operation (adding guest students). This mismatch can confuse students about the required API and cause compilation/test inconsistencies.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is required, implement it inside the method (or provide a clearly named separate method) rather than changing the public signature expected by the exercise.
